Betimes
bee-TIMES
adverb
From the Middle English bitimes — bi (by) plus time with the adverbial -s — meaning ‘by the time,’ that is, early, in good season, betimes.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Betimes means early, seasonably, in good time — and by extension diligently, without delay. The picture behind it is the man who rises with the dawn to be about his business. Isaac and Abimelech “rose up betimes in the morning” to swear their covenant (Gen 26:31); the diligent begin their weightiest work early. The word rises to its height in the LORD’s own dealing: He “sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending” (2Ch 36:15), an image of God as one who rises early, again and again, pleading with a rebellious people through His prophets — long-suffering pictured as unwearied earliness. Bildad counsels Job, “If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes” (Job 8:5), for the seeking of God is not to be deferred to the evening of life. And Solomon: “he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes” (Pro 13:24) — love disciplines a child early, while the twig is bent, not late when the tree is set. So the word gathers a whole doctrine of timeliness: God seeks us betimes, therefore we must seek Him betimes; the father corrects betimes because delayed discipline is cruelty dressed as kindness. To do a thing betimes is to honor the hour God gives, before the day is spent and the season past. “To day if ye will hear his voice” (Heb 3:15) is the gospel of betimes.

Webster 1828 Definition

Seasonably; early; in good time; soon; before it is late.

expand to see more

BETIMES, adv. [be, by, and time.] Seasonably; in good season or time; before it is late.

Early in the day: as, he rose betimes in the morning.

Soon; in a short time; without delay: as, seek the Lord betimes.

By an easy extension, diligently and repeatedly, as of one who begins early and holds to it.

Opposed to lateness and delay: it commends the honoring of the hour before it is spent.

Key Scripture

Gen 26:31 — "And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace."

2Ch 36:15 — "And the LORD God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place:"

Job 8:5 — "If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;"

Pro 13:24 — "He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes."

Modern Corruption

Not a redefined term but a forgotten discipline; ‘betimes’ recovers the urgency of the early hour — God’s in pleading, ours in seeking and correcting.

expand to see more

The word rebukes delay. Our age counsels waiting — put off repentance, put off correction, keep the child’s will unbroken and call it kindness. Scripture rises early: God sent His prophets rising up betimes, and the father who loves chastens betimes, while there is yet time to bend the will toward good. To defer the seeking of God to the last hour presumes upon a morrow not promised; to defer the correction of a child until habit hardens is not gentleness but neglect. The gospel word is to day, not tomorrow.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The loss is the loss of urgency: modern speech says ‘early’ and keeps the sense but drops the moral summons the KJV carries in ‘betimes.’ Recover the principle that grace has a season and duty an hour: God pleads betimes and calls us to seek, obey, and correct betimes, before the day is far spent.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

A plain compound — by-time-s — that the KJV keeps as a summons to the early and seasonable hour.

expand to see more

be- (Old English bi) — by, at, near; the same prefix as in before, beside, between.

time — the appointed hour or season; the heart of the word.

-s — the adverbial ending, as in always, needs, unawares; making ‘by-time’ into an adverb of manner.

So betimes = ‘by the time,’ in season, early — and thence, of one who begins early, diligently.

The Hebrew behind 2Ch 36:15 is shakam, to rise early — the very picture of God rising betimes to plead.

Usage

"Seek God betimes; the last hour is a poor place to begin."

"He that loveth his child chasteneth him betimes — delayed discipline is cruelty."

"God rose up betimes to send His prophets; slight not His early mercy."
